title: [C19T3] - The production of ethanol
prompt: The diagram below shows how a biofuel called ethanol is produced. Sumarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the cyclical process of manufacturing ethanol as a biofuel, from the initial growing of plants to the final product for transportation before being emitted to the environment.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, this is a continuous cycle where carbon dioxide is both absorbed and released throughout various stages. The process consists of six main stages, beginning with plant growth and ending with ethanol being used for different modes of transportation.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The process begins when plants and trees utilize energy from sunlight and carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to grow. These plants are then harvested using agricultural machinery before being transported to pre-processing facilities, where they are broken down into cellulose.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In the following stages, the cellulose undergoes chemical processing to produce sugars, which are then fed to microbes. The resultant chemical compound is then processed to create ethanol, which is used to power various forms of transportation, including cars, trucks, and aircraft. Finally, through the combustion of of ethanol as a source of fuel, carbon dioxide is released back into the atmosphere, where it becomes available for plants to use again, thus beginning the cycle once again.
